standard.title: Explain idea structures in texts
standard.description: Explain the structure of ideas such as the use of taxonomies, cause and effect, extended metaphors and chronology
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can select, navigate and read texts for a range of purposes, monitoring meaning and evaluating structural features (AC9E6LY04). They have not yet explicitly explained how ideas themselves are structured — the logical or rhetorical patterns (taxonomy, cause-effect, metaphor, chronology) that organise thinking within and across texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how ideas are structured using taxonomies, cause and effect, metaphors and chronology.

nodes.label: Idea structure patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and name the idea structure being used in a given text and explain how it organises the ideas
nodes.minimum_width: In a given text, identify the idea structure being used (taxonomy, cause-effect, extended metaphor, or chronology) and explain how it organises the information or argument
nodes.typical_width: Examine idea structures across different text types — taxonomies in scientific explanations, cause-effect in arguments and explanations, chronology in recounts and histories — and explain how the structure serves each text's purpose
wider: Identify cause and effect in explanations and analyse how causal structure is used to convince an audience of a course of action — tracing how the reasoning moves from cause to effect to recommended response
Examine how extended metaphors organise ideas in literary and persuasive texts — how a sustained comparison shapes the way readers understand a concept
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot recognise and name idea structures, Node 2's work on how structure serves purpose is inaccessible — explaining why a structure was chosen requires first being able to identify what structure is present.

response_modes.reason: Students need a working repertoire of idea structure patterns to recognise them across texts. Building knowledge of the four named structures — taxonomy, cause-effect, extended metaphor, chronology — across varied text examples gives students the analytical tools to explain how ideas are organised, not just describe what a text is about.

success_criteria: Identifies the idea structure in a given text (taxonomy, cause-effect, extended metaphor, or chronology)
Explains how the structure organises the ideas in that text

nodes.label: Idea structures serve purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the choice of idea structure in a text serves its purpose and shapes the reader's understanding
nodes.minimum_width: Explain why a specific idea structure is well-suited to a text's purpose — e.g. why cause-effect suits an explanation that aims to convince, or why chronology suits a recount
nodes.typical_width: Compare two texts on related topics that use different idea structures and explain how the different structures produce different understandings — what does a taxonomic organisation make visible that a chronological one obscures, or vice versa?
wider: Examine how a writer uses cause-effect structure not just to explain but to persuade — tracing how the causal chain is constructed to make a recommended action seem inevitable

Analyse how the same sequence of events can be structured as chronology (neutral recount) or cause-effect (persuasive argument) and discuss how the choice of structure shapes the reader's interpretation

response_modes.reason: Students can identify an idea structure without being able to explain why a writer chose it over alternatives. The reasoning scaffold — what does this structure make salient, what does it obscure, and how does that serve the purpose — builds the explanatory connection between structure choice and meaning-making that the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The cause-effect as persuasion direction is genuinely rich — advancing students can analyse how causal framing constructs inevitability, which connects linguistic analysis to critical and rhetorical awareness.
success_criteria: Explains why a specific idea structure suits the purpose of a given text
Identifies how the structure shapes the reader's understanding of the topic
